nodes.name: When a lead arrives
nodes.notes: Called by each source workflow (form, Gmail, webhook) with one normalised lead. All the thinking lives here so the sources stay thin.

nodes.name: Settings
nodes.notes: Everything that changes per client, in one visible place. n8n blocks environment variables inside nodes by default, and a Config node is easier to hand over than a hidden file.

nodes.name: Check the lead
nodes.notes: Normalises the lead and checks the one field that cannot be missing: a usable email address.

nodes.name: Send to quarantine
nodes.notes: No email means the lead cannot be deduplicated or answered. It is recorded with everything that arrived, and the owner is alerted.

nodes.name: Read the scoring criteria
nodes.notes: Read on EVERY lead, on purpose. The owner edits the document in plain English and the next lead is scored by the new rules - no developer, no deployment.

nodes.name: Turn the Doc into text
nodes.notes: Flattens Google's document tree to plain text, and refuses to continue if the criteria are empty.

nodes.name: Score the lead

parameters.text:
=You score incoming sales leads for a commercial cleaning company.

Score ONLY against the criteria below. They are written by the business owner and are the whole truth about what a good lead looks like. If the criteria and your instincts disagree, follow the criteria.

=== SCORING CRITERIA ===
{{ $json.criteria }}
=== END OF CRITERIA ===

=== THE LEAD ===
{{ JSON.stringify($json.lead, null, 2) }}
=== END OF LEAD ===

Rules:
- Score 1 to 10 using the criteria's own bands.
- The tier must match the score using the criteria's thresholds.
- The reason is ONE sentence that quotes real details from this lead, so a salesperson can judge it without opening anything else.
- Never invent facts. If the lead does not say how big the premises are, do not guess - score what is there and say what is missing.
- The suggested action is one short instruction, e.g. "Call today and offer a walkthrough".

nodes.notes:
One shot: criteria in, score out. No tools and no memory, because each lead is judged on its own.

If Groq is down or refuses, this node does NOT stop the pipeline: the lead continues as 'unscored' and still reaches the CRM. A scoring outage must never cost the business a lead.

nodes.name: Groq model
nodes.notes: Temperature 0: the same lead must always get the same score, or the owner cannot trust the numbers.

nodes.name: Force the JSON shape
nodes.notes: The shape is enforced here rather than trusted from the prompt. autoFix gives one repair attempt before the lead is treated as unscored.

nodes.name: Repair model
nodes.notes: Only runs when the first reply is not valid JSON. Reconciling broken JSON against a schema is a coding task, so it gets its own call.

nodes.name: Check the score
nodes.notes: The tier is recalculated from the score, and an unusable answer becomes 'unscored' rather than a lost lead.

nodes.name: Say why it failed

assignments.name: error
assignments.value: No usable email address, so the lead cannot be deduplicated or replied to.

nodes.notes: The quarantine row is only useful if it says what went wrong. Without this, every rejected lead reads 'unknown step / no reason given'.
